purpose: Enforce the fail-closed Rust behavior for current candidates, independent verification, exact evidence, computed verdict transitions, and bounded precise rework.

rustTarget.note: The rule audit always runs. Named Rust modules and tests become mandatory once the phase 2.4 candidate module exists. Canonical Rust modules must use ProductSession, ExecutionJob, WorkerSession, CodexThread, and WorkRun identities and must not restore the retired TypeScript domain or legacy session fields.

implementationBoundary.phase24DomainPolicy: Phase 2.4 is a fail-closed Rust domain and application layer. It defines sealed validated fact types, checks their identity, ordering, candidate, role, outcome, and rework relationships, derives Candidate, Evidence, Verdict, and Attention, and persists WorkRun, Attention, and Verdict changes only through operation-specific sealed transitions. Public commands, API DTOs, raw snapshots, and raw Worker messages cannot construct a sealed fact or relabel a derived transition.
implementationBoundary.productionEnablementPolicy: A domain unit test may create sealed fixtures through crate-private test support. Production candidate freeze, evidence resolution, verification settlement, verdict computation, and replacement-candidate acceptance remain unavailable until the owning adapters below produce the required sealed facts and pass their integration gates; a domain test is not proof that Git, an Artifact, a checkout, or a runtime event was actually verified.

adapterDependencies.produces: A sealed base/candidate commit-to-tree resolution, exact diff digest, changed paths, path object IDs, and pre/post verification or rework snapshots read from the exact Job workspace or immutable Artifact.

adapterDependencies.owner: Phase 2.3 stage coordinator and Worker outcome adapter
adapterDependencies.produces: A sealed terminal outcome matched to WorkRun, ExecutionJob, attempt, Lease, fencing token, Worker, Worker instance, WorkerSession, CodexThread, status, and lastEventSequence.

adapterDependencies.owner: ExecutionPort ingestion and append-only runtime ledger adapter
adapterDependencies.produces: A sealed durable source position plus its original type, identity, time, sequence, candidate provenance, and direct outcome loaded from the accepted runtime ledger.

adapterDependencies.owner: Execution Worker checkout and Artifact adapter
adapterDependencies.produces: A sealed ExecutionJob checkout commit/tree attestation matched to the current attempt, Lease, fence, Worker instance, WorkerSession, and immutable candidate Artifact.

candidate.factSourcePolicy: The phase 2.4 domain freezes only a sealed ValidatedGitSnapshotFact and matching VerifiedTerminalOutcome/ValidatedCheckoutAttestationFact. The owning adapters rebuild and attest those facts for the exact SessionBinding and successful Worker outcome; the domain checks their complete bindings and cannot itself read Git, a Worker workspace, or an Artifact. Format-valid caller strings or an unmatched Worker artifact are not candidate facts.

evidence.sourcePolicy: EvidenceRef stores a bounded source reference. Resolution must find one unique earlier accepted source fact whose type, role, ProductSession, ExecutionJob, WorkerSession, CodexThread, WorkRun, attempt, lease, fence, Worker instance, source sequence, and candidate all match canonical Control Plane state; it never copies complete logs or command output.
evidence.candidateCheckoutPolicy: Runtime test, command, file, diff, commit, and review evidence can support a candidate only when the phase 2.4 domain receives a sealed ValidatedCheckoutAttestationFact whose commit and tree match that frozen candidate. The Worker/Artifact adapter creates that proof; Stage timing or an optional candidateRef string is not proof of the checkout.
evidence.ledgerPolicy: Verdict commands reference already persisted source positions. They do not carry caller-provided runtime event bodies, timestamps, outcomes, or source sequences. The runtime-ledger adapter loads and seals AcceptedRuntimeSourceFact values; the phase 2.4 domain only validates and derives from those facts.

verification.assignmentPolicy: For the current candidate, every required role resolves to exactly one current assignment consisting of one role-scoped WorkRun and one complete SessionBinding. Zero or multiple assignments for a role fail closed before findings are considered.
verification.sessionPolicy: Reviewer and Verifier each use exactly one current role-scoped WorkRun and exactly one complete SessionBinding, distinct from the candidate writer and from one another. Ambiguous current runs or bindings fail closed.
verification.candidateIntegrityPolicy: Every verification run starts and ends on the same frozen candidate commit, tree, and diff. The GitSnapshotResolver/Artifact adapter seals the pre/post facts; the phase 2.4 domain compares them and invalidates a changed snapshot even when no recognized file-write event was emitted.
verification.terminalPolicy: A role settles only when its canonical WorkRun succeeded and the phase 2.4 domain receives a sealed VerifiedTerminalOutcome that matches its SessionBinding, ExecutionJob, attempt, lease, fence, Worker, instance, WorkerSession, and CodexThread. The structured result and every supporting source sequence must not exceed the outcome lastEventSequence. A runtime final message cannot settle a running WorkRun.

verdict.computedBy: The Rust phase 2.4 domain computes from current canonical Delivery state and sealed validated facts supplied by trusted ports; it does not fetch Git or Worker data itself. Callers and Workers do not submit EvidenceRef, CriterionResult, DeliveryVerdict, or sealed fact objects.
verdict.requiredRoleAgreementPolicy: Pass and product fail require current direct evidence from every required role and one consistent product outcome. A missing, incomplete, or inconclusive role keeps the criterion inconclusive; a required role infrastructure failure remains infra_error and is not overwritten by another role product-fail message.

rework.afterWriterStarts: The previous candidate immediately stops being current. Historical evidence may remain append-only, but it cannot authorize a new pass, review, or publication.
rework.resultPolicy: The remediator replacement candidate must remain inside the approved WorkItem, file, and hunk boundaries. The GitSnapshotResolver/Artifact adapter seals the resulting snapshot; the phase 2.4 domain compares it with the authorization and rejects any added path or out-of-bound hunk. Prompt wording alone is not enforcement.
rework.attemptSequenceSource: distinct earlier failed candidates in the append-only current DeliverySpec verdict history

rules.statement: A frozen candidate is a deterministic derived value bound to the current DeliverySpec, repository baseline, one succeeded executor or remediator WorkRun including task, stage, role, and attempt, its exact complete ProductSession/ExecutionJob/WorkerSession/CodexThread SessionBinding, and exact Git commit, tree, diff, and changed-path facts.

The candidate Git snapshot is rebuilt through a trusted resolver: base and candidate commits resolve to the stated trees, their exact diff hashes to diffSha256, and its paths and object IDs equal changedPaths. Format-valid caller strings cannot become a candidate.

Candidate freezing requires the exact accepted successful Worker outcome for the producer SessionBinding and a Git snapshot read from that outcome Job workspace. A succeeded WorkRun flag, a caller snapshot, or an artifact from another job, attempt, lease, fence, Worker instance, or WorkerSession is insufficient.
A frozen candidate is stale after its spec identity or facts change, or as soon as a later executing or reworking writer WorkRun starts, whether that writer is running or finished.
Reviewer and Verifier are both mandatory verification roles; a caller cannot remove either role, while an adversarial verifier remains an optional additional role.

Reviewer and Verifier each bind exactly one current role-scoped verification WorkRun to exactly one complete SessionBinding; both are distinct from the candidate writer and from one another, and ambiguous duplicate runs or bindings fail closed.
Every Reviewer, Verifier, and required adversarial verifier uses the canonical candidate-read-only workspace policy and a restricted runtime permission profile.

Any candidate mutation during Reviewer, Verifier, or Adversarial Verifier execution invalidates that verification result. The pre/post commit, tree, and diff must remain exact even when the mutation came from a command or another event not classified as a file or patch write.

A verification role settles only after its canonical WorkRun succeeded and one accepted terminal Worker outcome matches the complete current SessionBinding and fenced job attempt; a completed model turn cannot settle a still-running WorkRun.
Every persisted EvidenceRef identifies the current Delivery and exact current DeliverySpec identity and revision.

Every persisted EvidenceRef and every CriterionResult that cites it identify the exact current candidate; evidence for a prior or foreign candidate stays historical and cannot enter the current verdict.
Every EvidenceRef identifies one existing Codex WorkRun in the same Delivery, and a verification source must consume the producer candidate for the same DeliveryTask scope.
Every EvidenceRef identifies one SessionBinding for its WorkRun, with complete session identities and a binding time that does not follow the evidence or predate the run.

A runtime EvidenceRef resolves to exactly one earlier accepted source fact whose source type, ProductSession, ExecutionJob, WorkerSession, CodexThread, WorkRun, role, attempt, lease, fencing token, Worker, Worker instance, source sequence, and candidate identity all agree with canonical Control Plane state.

The persisted source occurrence time and sequence must be at or after the WorkRun start and SessionBinding time, earlier than its finding and verdict, and no later than the accepted terminal Worker outcome lastEventSequence. Callers cannot replace or raise the source time.

The runtime-ledger adapter reads source bodies, timestamps, outcomes, and sequences only from the Control Plane accepted append-only ledger and seals an AcceptedRuntimeSourceFact. Callers submit bounded source positions, not RuntimeEvent objects; the phase 2.4 domain accepts only that sealed fact.

A runtime test, command, file, diff, commit, or finding can support the current candidate only when its accepted ExecutionJob checkout commit and tree attestation exactly match that candidate; sharing a WorkRun time window or omitting candidateRef never establishes candidate provenance.
A pass or fail CriterionResult cites at least one current EvidenceRef; inconclusive and infra_error may be evidence-free when the missing or failed verification state itself is the reason.

An Agent message, final response, review_finding, or generic runtime_event cannot be the sole direct support for pass; every required role must cite a current test, command, diff, file, or commit fact that the Control Plane resolved independently.

The Control Plane derives product failure, infrastructure failure, and success from resolved direct outcomes. An Agent cannot relabel a failed product check as infra_error, a successful declared check as fail, or an infrastructure failure as a product result.
A criterion whose approved verificationMethod is missing remains verification-blocked and inconclusive; Reviewer or Verifier text cannot invent a convenient check and turn it into pass.

Pass or product fail requires current direct evidence from every required role and one consistent product outcome. One role fail cannot override another role missing, incomplete, inconclusive, or infrastructure-failed state.

Public commands never accept caller- or Worker-created EvidenceRef, CriterionResult, DeliveryVerdict, status, or Attention values. The Rust Control Plane rebuilds them from the current Delivery and accepted source facts before one atomic write.
The current DeliveryVerdict evaluates every current acceptance criterion exactly once and includes no duplicate or foreign criterion.
A missing, waiting, running, or incomplete required Reviewer or Verifier Session produces an inconclusive CriterionResult and cannot open the pass path.
A settled finding without enough current direct evidence is inconclusive, records an evidence-mismatch finding, and cannot be changed into pass by the role message.

Different current Reviewer and Verifier product conclusions for the same criterion preserve both findings, create a deterministic conflict record, and produce inconclusive; one role product-fail message cannot override the other role pass, missing, incomplete, or inconclusive state.

A failed or cancelled required verification Session, or timed-out, policy-denied, infrastructure-failed, or cancelled supporting execution, produces infra_error rather than pass, fail, or generic inconclusive.
A finding that claims pass while its cited test or command failed is an evidence mismatch and becomes inconclusive; an observed failed check can never support pass.

Precise rework is accepted only for the current reviewed candidate, exact diff, original DeliveryTask scope, visible diagram node, changed file, exact hunk digest, and current candidate-bound evidence references; the replacement candidate must also prove that its resulting diff stayed within those approved boundaries.

After a remediator finishes, the replacement Git snapshot must show that every changed path and hunk remains inside the approved DeliveryTask, file, and hunk authorization. Prompt instructions or valid input annotations alone do not authorize an expanded result.

When one verdict produces multiple blocking Attention items, the next Delivery state is recomputed from the complete current action set with clarification ahead of rework and rework ahead of verification retry. Resolution order or the last item cannot weaken that transition.

A rework writer is a Codex remediator, the Control Plane derives its next attempt from all current-Delivery reworking WorkRuns, and the number of rework WorkRuns never exceeds the approved DeliverySpec maximum.

The next business rework ordinal is one plus the number of distinct earlier failed candidates in the append-only current DeliverySpec verdict history, across WorkItems. Execution retries and historical WorkRuns do not reset or increment that business ordinal; the history proof must match the exact Delivery revision.

Starting a new remediator writer immediately makes the previous frozen candidate non-current; the replacement binds a new WorkRun and SessionBinding and must repeat Reviewer, Verifier, evidence, and verdict computation.
When the approved rework limit is exhausted or the same criterion fails again after rework, the next action is definition clarification instead of another automatic code rework.
